title: Bring the Ruckus
description:
This place is pretty fun so far, despite all the dry political talk. I know Saltheril is trying to get the nobles to buy up war bonds, but we could really use some more energy in here. If the nobles are all asleep, no one's buying anything.

Tell you what. Go invite some of my friends. They hang out under the bridge right outside of Silvermoon's gates.

If anyone can bring some energy to the soiree, it's us.
completion:
The energy's high, the drinks are flowing, and people are having a good time!

That's how you start making deals.

title: One Smuggler to Another
description:
The whole point of this deal is showing the nobles what we bring to the table, both for Silvermoon and for them personally.

These other groups bring strength, power, and really nice armor. What we bring is resources: getting the sin'dorei what they need, when they need it, with no questions asked.

I heard some folks over at Sunsail Anchorage have been trying out the same business, but they're putting gold in the wrong pockets. Swipe their stock and bring it here.
progress: I don't mind competitors, but I don't like the deals those smugglers are making.
completion: If there's anything good in these crates, we'll get it on the market.

title: Dangerous Showpieces
description:
You'd be surprised at the money you can make off of weapons. No, not the kind you're meant to use--the kind you stick up on the wall and have conversations about.

Usually those weapons are expensive, or dangerous, or otherwise hard to get your hands on. The more rare and exclusive, the better.

The weapons those Twilight cultists are carrying around should sell pretty well, especially to buyers with edgier tastes. If you happen to come across any, I'll gladly take them off your hands.
progress: If it has some blood on it, that's actually better.
completion: Nice work. Eversong is safer because of your heroism, and I get to pocket a little more gold. I'd call that a win-win.

title: Artisanal Replicas
description:
Don't let the austere demeanor fool you. Nobles are just as susceptible to flashy party favors as the rest of us.

I had my people bring over a batch of Felo'melorn replicas. They look great on display, and even better--they're enchanted. Swing them around and they leave a trail of fire.

I haven't sold an enchanted batch before, so I'd like to do some testing before I hand them out. Saltheril wouldn't be too happy if I burned a guest to a crisp.

Wanna take one of the replicas for a test run?
completion:
I told you they were flashy!

Sounds like the enchantment could get tuned down a little bit, but where's the fun in that?

description:
I feel like I just got here and I'm already fresh out of half the poisons I brought.

What? Don't look at me like that. Nobles are some of my top customers for poisons. Quieter than magic and cleaner than blades.

I need to restock. The frogs way down in the south produce a poisonous slime that I can bottle without much fuss. Bring some of it to me and I'll get you a cut of the earnings.

completion:
Excellent. That's enough to restock what I've sold and then some.

Oh, by the way, you probably want to wash your hands. Maybe a few times.

description:
We've been making friends with some of the guests by teaching them how to play dice. It's a nice way to draw people out of the crowd and get them in a quieter space where you can talk privately.

I wasn't expecting so much interest, to be honest. We're running out of dice sets.

I can carve some more, but I'll need materials. Usually teeth or bone are good picks. Actually, the fangs from those naga along the coast would be perfect. Now that's a conversation starter!

I need to stay here and play politics, but could you head over to Tranquillien and grab a few bottles? I'll give you a list.

objectives: Dig up the Concealed Dirt Mound
description:
The oldest trick in the book is to create a problem on purpose, solve it yourself, and look like the hero.

One of the nobles just got word that some prized valuable was stolen from their estate while they were occupied here. It just so happens I might have put one of their servants up to it.

Go talk to a man named Seridis over at the livery. He'll hand over the valuable to you, then you'll come back here and pretend you valiantly subdued the thief and retrieved the item.

Everyone's happy.
progress: Making friends with the servants in noble households opens up a lot of doors. Sometimes literally.
completion:
Look at that. Everyone comes out a winner!

The noble gets his valuable back unscathed, Seridis gets paid handsomely, and you and I look brave and capable in front of the soiree.

title: Graveblossom Gardening
description:
My colleague Amalthea has taken ill. She requires a specialized poultice of sorts in order to ease the symptoms. I would forage for the plants myself, but the local fauna have grown so testy as of late!

While you are out and about, could you gather some graveblossoms for me? I'd happily make it worth your while.
progress:
Oh, come now. While we stand here and chat about the weather, my associate continues to suffer under the travails of her malady! Get on with it.

It's gloomy, by the way. The weather. As usual.
completion:
There you have it! Eight flowers. Simple enough, no? Now, I just need a few more things...

What? I didn't mention that there would be a shopping list? Oh, bother. Well, nothing to it but to do it now, hrm? You don't seem the type to leave things half-handled.

title: A Venomous Vocation
description:
My poultice requires venom samples from the local giant bat populations. Please retrieve some of those, as well. Six common vials' worth should do.

Don't give me that look. They're bats. There are mad Light-plant-things to the east and a storm of voidwalkers swirling over our heads. Don't you dare give me guff about the dangers of big, fluffy bats. Now shoo. My colleague is depending on your prompt and efficient aid.
progress: Strictly speaking, a stronger venom would have a more ample effect. But we're living in strenuous times. This Void hooplah has my usual supply lines at Sunsail completely occupied. We'll have to make do with mournbat venom. Now go.
completion: There we are. See? I knew I could rely on you. We've only a few steps left to manage.

title: House Call
description:
I thought Barrem was lost to us after the tragedy at Broken Shore, Light knows we lost far too many good soldiers just like him there.

I was shocked to see he was still alive when one of our patrols arrived carrying him. They found him floating in the sea with wounds that would kill any lesser draenei.

There is something about those wounds that resists everything we've done to treat them. Please, priest, as a brother in the Light I ask you to do all that you can to help him to recover.
completion:
I... I owe you my life, , but that look on your face tells me you're here for something else.

I must have been dreaming of Alora, she was my cell mate in that accursed world the demons took me to. She told me she saw the crystal but never said much else.

I just hope she is still alive.

title: Flowers for Amalthea
completion:
Goodness! That was nearly quite the misunderstanding. I am glad you stayed your weapons long enough to hear me out.

The Scourge took much from the sin'dorei. For some, like Amalthea, it took everything and more.

Needless to say, my studies don't get me invited to many parties. But they allow me, from time to time, to ease Amalthea's torment. To that end, I would bear any indignity.

title: Murloc Madness
description:
These murlocs have come to me, the Loa of Murlocs, to seek my protection against an evil invader.

The Deepfin have risen from the abyssal depths of the ocean. They have invaded this land and defiled its grounds!

I charge you, champion, to defend this kingdom and drive the Deepfin back into the sea!

Get rid of the invaders and maybe the natives won't need me to protect them, and I can leave!
progress: I await your victorious return!
completion:
Are you finished?

I mean, it is finished. The Deepfin shall trouble us no more!

title: Fish Are Food, Not Friends
description:
I have heard your mrgls, my people. Your stomachs grgl in hunger!

The invaders have cut you off from the food you so desperately need to survive.

I will send my champion to gather fish so you may fill your bellies once more!

Or you can just give me fish if you have some?

title: Following Suit
description:
My fellow murlocs! One among you was chosen to be my... my chosen!

She is destined for greatness and is my assistant... erm, priestess! Yes, priestess of the loa!

Your priestess has gone missing, possibly taken by the treacherous Deepfin.

To showcase my great power, I will send my champion to find and return her to you.

My assistant is missing, and I'm stuck here! Find her and tell her I'm on top of the temple!
progress: ! I command you to return my priestess unharmed.

title: One Hero's Prey
objectives: Prey target selected on the Hunt Table
description:
Again, we sin'dorei find our city under assault. And again, it is up to the finer minds among us to come to Silvermoon's aid.

Mortal anguish, it seems, is a powerful reflection of the soul. When contained and manipulated, anguish acts as a form of magic that we can wield to protect this great city.

I've located a number of anguish-filled targets across Azeroth.

Select and hunt one such target, storing their anguish in this crystalline vessel. Then return to me.
progress: Who would have known this power was here all along, ripe for the taking?
completion: While you collect more anguish, I will experiment with this power's potential.

title: Precious Jewels
description:
...

While you've been away, I've been refining our work.

Small trinkets and jewelry that contain crystallized anguish.

I've discretely gifted these to a few willing Silvermoon citizens. I wish to observe the effect of a controlled concentration of anguish over time.

I've shaped the magic to lend the bearer health and strength. Seek our volunteers out and check up on them.
progress: My work here will make the world fear Silvermoon's might.
completion:
Aggression is simply an expression of strength.

So long as we are the predator, not the prey.

... I need you to attend to a matter in the city.

I've received word from Knight Captain Solara that there's been an incident in the Gardens of Remembrance. She reports elves have begun acting out violently, causing coalesced anguish to manifest and terrorize the residents.

You can use the crystalline vessel to reclaim the coalesced anguish and soothe the elves whose minds have crumbled.

So much of the magic will weigh heavy upon you, but I'm confident you have the strength.
progress: In all of my endeavors, there are always some who seek to impede my progress.
completion: There will always be some who resist progress, but no matter the cost, my studies in anguish are for the people of Silvermoon.

The materials we need are far more bespoke than I keep in my shop, however. We'll need to source our manasilk directly--fortunately, it isn't far. Just outside the city gates.

Dat is superstition, but dat's why she's goin'.

We lost her twin, Janaka. She must think she's with Filo.

I thought de murlocs were driven into their frenzy by de trinkets, but they're just baubles made by de snakes. Once we drew closer to dat lighthouse, I began to suspect dey were not de cause.

I can feel it from here. A pulsing darkness. Ancient. If you go up there, you may find de true source of de murlocs' madness.

Your time was not wasted in gathering de trinkets. We were able to narrow down de source once we ruled them out!

That aside, I have never felt anything like de ripples of darkness coming from dat tower. Find and destroy whatever it is dat's controlling de murlocs.

So de murloc chieftain had a shadow-filled crystal? I wonder...

It is possible dat de murlocs unearthed dis ancient relic and dat its power consumed dem. A pity it was destroyed. I would have liked to study it.

Ndamu is a great loss, but de work you did here today means her sacrifice was not in vain. De snakes have been dealt a solid blow, de murlocs should start calming down, and we destroyed de source of de dark energy. Thank you, .

At least, that's what Doru calls them: echoes. All I see are ghosts of a bloodier time. And like those days, no matter how many we cut through, they never stop swarming in.

Dey were not honorable fighters for us to challenge ourselves against, such as yourself. They were vermin--greedy opportunists that drove legions of connivin' adventurers to rob us of our possessions, our treasures, and... our tusks.

Slayin' de echoes of these key figures should reduce de number of echoes appearin'.

And it will make me grin to know they've fallen.

Can ya believe de instigators even returned years later when de Zandalari propped their puppet leader up?

"Immortal," my rear...

Poison de feasts dey find respite at, hex their disrespectful civilian allies, and sabotage dat chest they seem so keen on lootin'!

I cannot ask this of any Amani. Or Witherbark, Revantusk, or Shadowpine. Ya presence with us in these times must be fate... Because we could only make this request to an outsider.

Ya must inhabit a soul of de profane ones--Those that accepted Malacrass' vile bargain and consumed Loa power during de era of Zul'jin.

Return to de shrine of de profane one ya wish to merge with.

Ancestors forgive us...

We are grateful Akil'zon opened our eyes to de truth of Zul'jin and Malacrass's dark deeds.

Even if it means we accept their shame as our own.

Thank you, hash'ura. Truly.

The battle against de echoes will continue. However, it would seem they cannot return after being slain now that their leader has been dealt with.

Memories stirred my blood these last few days. Now we can all rest. Perhaps even move on?

Bah! It's just de ravin' of an old warrior. Do not mind me.

We have traced Ruia's flight through the Rootways. As we suspected, he has sought refuge deep within The Blinding Vale, where the Lightbloom first took root within Harandar.

Ruia's demise is a tragedy. You never knew him as such, but he was once a man of honor and conviction. To think that the light would blind him so completely to the folly of his ambitions...

Our arcane constructs might look purely magical, but there's quite a bit of advanced wiring going on beneath the surface. Silvermoon's engineers truly are spell-workers in their own right.

title: Learning the Cloaks - Part 1
description:
In this game of Decor Duel, one side uses illusion to disguise themselves as, and hide amongst, everyday objects in the area.

The other side uses pre-approved lists of illusion-piercing abilities to find and then capture those hiding cloaked in disguise.

At the end of the round, the teams switch roles, so each side has a chance to hide and seek.

Time for you to try! This armchair has been enchanted to cloak you with its disguise. Don its appearance, then change your disguise a few times.
progress: Touch this armchair, to don its disguise...
completion:
You took to that like a cloak to concealment. Well done!

But, in this game, a good disguise or hiding spot isn't always enough. There is much more for you to learn.

title: Learning the Cloaks - Part 2
description:
When disguised, you will have the ability to magically teleport yourself to a nearby piece of decor.

Pick up the chair's disguise again, and this time try swapping your location a few times. Feel free to change your disguise between swaps if you'd like.
progress: Use the disguise chair to swap with other decor, then return to me.
completion:
Nicely done! But that's only half the game, isn't it.

Next, let's get you exposed to some Capturing tactics. If you think you can handle it, of course.

title: Nothing Captured, Nothing Gained
objectives: Get outfited with the Spellbreaker kit
Use Dispelling Focus to find hiders (3)
description:
There are three Seeker classes in Decor Duel, but everyone starts off with the Spellbreaker kit. Don't worry--you can earn access to the others.

Some fundamentals: you can break the shield of a disguised hider's illusion by using Dispel Magic. Once the hider has been marked as Found, you'll have a brief window to Tag them, taking them out of the match.

My statue has been enchanted to outfit you with a Spellbreaker kit. Once outfitted, use Dispel Magic to find and tag decoys hiding around here.
progress: Use my statue, then find and tag hiders with the Spellbreaker's Dispel Magic and Tag.
completion: Not bad for a first time. You're taking to this quite naturally!

The war effort has been taxing on Silvermoon's resources. We need to keep our soldiers armed and supplied, but even our seasoned crafters have been overwhelmed. To keep up with demand, we have struck a deal with the Artisan's Consortium.

If you have your own skills to offer, speak to Mar'nah. She can help you view and place crafting orders.

To the north, you will find Har'kuai. The rains that fall from the sky there carry a remarkable vitality. If you wish to witness all of Aln'hara's majesties, then a trek to Har'kuai would serve you well.

I have heard of your travels, outsider. I am Kamari, Rootwarden of Nordrassil.

They're looking for new participants to help spread the entertainment.

You should meet them over in Falconwing Square.

title: Har'mara, Village of Balance
description:
Ah! The outsider who saved Har'mara. Word travels fast through Aln'hara's roots. No doubt Elder Hagar was grateful for your aid.

She would never admit it, but things have been difficult since the roots above her village burned. The rutaani and fungarians each grow bolder in their eccentricities. And the lingering flare-ups on Teldrassil's roots present a constant threat.

If your travels afford another trip to Har'mara, I do not doubt she would benefit from additional help.
completion:
Ah! . Welcome back. As you can see, our hands are full as ever, here.

I assure you, I have things well in hand. But if you do wish to explore a bit further afield, I am sure some of the others could benefit from your assistance.

Our efforts in the Blinding Bloom have halted the Lightbloom's encroachment for now. But with Rootwarden Ruia gone, there are scarce few who remain to handle the rest of the village's troubles.

I'm going back to Har'alnor to help out where I can. If you have the time and the inclination, your further assistance would be most appreciated.

Thank the goddess you returned.

As you can see, we're still in fairly dire straits here. Though we quelled its spread beneath Shaladrassil's roots, the Lightbloom remains a threat. There are rumors of fungarians acting erratically in Fungara Village. And there is no Rootwarden in Har'alnor to deal with either.
